'''Derek''' Dek '''Woolfson''' FRS (born 7 July 1965) is a British [[chemist]] and [[biochemist]]. He is a professor of chemistry and biochemistry at the [[University of Bristol]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bristol |first=University of |title=Professor Dek Woolfson - School of Chemistry |url=http://www.bris.ac.uk/chemistry/people/dek-n-woolfson/ |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=www.bris.ac.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bristol |first=University of |title=Professor Dek Woolfson - Biochemistry |url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/biochemistry/people/dek-n-woolfson/index.html |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=www.bris.ac.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref> and professor of protein design at the [[University of Copenhagen]], where he is also Director of the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design.<ref name="KUstaff">{{Cite web |title=Derek N. Woolfson – Staff profile |url=https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/staff/?pure=en/persons/823974 |website=University of Copenhagen |access-date=2025-01-27 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="CPD">{{Cite web |title=Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design |url=https://cpd.ku.dk/ |website=University of Copenhagen |access-date=2025-01-27 |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Woolfson was born on 7 July 1965 in [[Birmingham]], UK. He attended [[King's Norton Boys' School]] (1976–1983). Woolfson was awarded a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[chemistry]] from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1987, doing undergraduate research with [[Chris Dobson|Christopher M. Dobson]]. He obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in chemistry and [[biochemistry]] from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1991 under the supervision of Prof. [[Dudley Williams (biochemist)|D. H. Williams]] (chemistry) and Dr. P. A. Evans (biochemistry).

== Career ==
Woolfson undertook post-doctoral research at [[University College London]] (1991–1992), and at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1992–1994), before accepting a [[Lecturer|Lectureship]] in Biochemistry at the University of Bristol from 1994 to 1995.

The following year, Woolfson was appointed Lecturer and later Professor of Biochemistry at the [[University of Sussex]], where he worked until 2005. Since 2005, Woolfson has held a joint chair between the Schools of Chemistry and Biochemistry at the [[University of Bristol]].

Woolfson was Principal Investigator and Director of the [[UK Research and Innovation|UKRI]]-funded Synthetic Biology Research Centre, BrisSynBio,<ref>{{Cite web |title=BrisSynBio – A BBSRC/EPSRC Synthetic Biology Research Centre |url=https://www.bristol.ac.uk/brissynbio/ |website=University of Bristol |access-date=2025-01-27 |language=en}}</ref> at the [[University of Bristol]]. He was Director of the Bristol BioDesign Institute<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bristol BioDesign Institute |url=https://www.bristol.ac.uk/biodesign-institute/ |website=University of Bristol |access-date=2025-01-27 |language=en}}</ref> at the University of Bristol and Founding Director of the [[Max Planck Society|Max Planck]]–Bristol Centre for Minimal Biology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Max Planck Bristol Centre for Minimal Biology |url=https://www.bristol.ac.uk/max-planck-bristol-centre/ |website=University of Bristol |access-date=2025-01-27 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry – Max Planck Bristol Centre for Minimal Biology |url=https://www.biochem.mpg.de/7587324/max-planck-bristol-centre |website=Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry |access-date=2025-01-27 |language=en}}</ref> In 2025, he took up a professorship in protein design at the [[University of Copenhagen]] and established the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design.<ref name="CPD"/>

== Research ==
Woolfson applies chemical and physical methods and principles to understand biological phenomena, such as [[protein folding]] and stability.

He is interested in how weak non-covalent interactions determine the structures and functions of [[protein]]s;<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Woolfson|first1=D. The current focuses of his group<ref>{{Cite web|title=Woolfson Group|url=https://woolfsonlab.wordpress.com/|access-date=2020-06-29|website=Woolfson Group|language=en}}</ref> are in the parametric design of protein structures, assemblies and materials; and in porting these into living cells to augment natural biology.
